items.name: Amla Chutney
steps: Steam the deseeded amla for four to five minutes until it yields to a fingernail; this softens the astringency without losing the sour rasa.
Dry-roast the cumin until fragrant.
Grind everything to a coarse paste with a little water, adding the jaggery last so the sourness stays forward.
Rest for ten minutes before serving; it keeps three days refrigerated.
items.guidance: Amla is the rare sour that cools rather than heats, which is why this chutney suits pitta where a tamarind or lime one would not. Vata: keep the chili low and add a spoon of sesame oil. Pitta: omit the chili entirely. Kapha: skip the jaggery.

items.name: Sol Kadhi
steps: Soak the kokum in 200 ml warm water for fifteen minutes and press out a deep pink extract.
Blend the coconut with 300 ml warm water and strain firmly to get thick coconut milk.
Crush the garlic, chili and cumin to a paste and stir into the coconut milk.
Combine with the kokum extract, salt lightly, and finish with coriander. Serve cool, never boiled — heat splits it.
items.guidance: The Konkan answer to a heavy or fried meal: kokum is sour but sheeta, so it settles pitta rather than provoking it, and the coconut carries it. Vata: serve at room temperature. Pitta: leave out the garlic. Kapha: thin the coconut milk and take a small cup.

items.name: Date Banana Smoothie
steps: Soak the dates in a little warm milk for ten minutes to soften.
Blend everything until completely smooth.
Serve at room temperature rather than chilled — cold blunts agni and this is already a heavy drink.
viruddhaFlags: milk with fruit is a contested combination; banana and milk are named together in some modern viruddha lists though not in the samhitas
items.guidance: Strongly building, and the classic vata breakfast when appetite is weak but weight is needed. Vata: as written. Pitta: reduce the dates. Kapha: this is the wrong drink — take warm spiced water instead.
provenance: modern preparation; ingredients per Bhavaprakasha Kharjura and Kadali

items.name: Amla Ginger Morning Shot
steps: Juice the amla and ginger together, or blend with 50 ml water and strain.
Let it come to room temperature before stirring in the honey — honey must never be added to anything hot.
Add the pepper and drink immediately; amla juice oxidises within minutes.
viruddhaFlags: honey must not be heated or added to a warm liquid
items.guidance: Taken on an empty stomach. The pepper is there for absorption, not heat. Vata: halve the ginger and follow with warm water. Pitta: omit the ginger and pepper. Kapha: as written. Not for children under twelve months because of the honey.
provenance: modern rasayana practice; amalaki per Charaka Samhita Chikitsasthana 1

items.name: Gond Ladoo
steps: Fry the gond in ghee over low heat until each piece puffs white and crisp; lift out and crush coarsely.
In the same ghee roast the flour on low heat until it darkens and smells nutty, twelve to fifteen minutes.
Take off the heat, fold in the jaggery while the mixture is warm but not hot, then the gond, almonds, dry ginger and cardamom.
Shape into ladoos while warm enough to hold.
items.guidance: A winter and postpartum food, brimhana and vata-pacifying, traditionally one a day with warm milk. Heavy by design. Vata: as written. Pitta: reduce the dry ginger. Kapha: not indicated. Not for weak agni or high ama.
provenance: North Indian winter and postpartum tradition

items.name: Samak Rice Bowl (Fasting)
steps: Rinse the samak and soak fifteen minutes.
Temper cumin and chili in ghee, add the potato and cook until it takes colour.
Add the drained samak and twice its volume of water; cook covered until soft, about twelve minutes.
Fold in the peanuts and coriander; rest five minutes before serving.
items.guidance: The vrat staple — samak is a millet, not a grain, which is why it is allowed on fasting days. Lighter than rice and easier on kapha. Vata: extra ghee and serve hot. Pitta: keep the chili out. Kapha: reduce the peanuts.

items.name: Singhara Flour Pakora
steps: Whisk the singhara flour with salt, pepper and cumin and enough water for a coating batter; rest ten minutes.
Dip the potato slices and fry in moderately hot oil until pale gold — singhara flour browns faster than gram flour.
Drain well and serve hot with a fasting-friendly chutney.
items.guidance: A vrat snack. Fried and therefore guru whatever the flour, so occasional rather than habitual. Vata: as written, eaten hot. Pitta: reduce the pepper and avoid in grishma. Kapha: not indicated.

items.name: Ugadi Pachadi
steps: Dissolve the jaggery and tamarind in 200 ml water and strain.
Stir in the raw mango, neem flowers, chili and salt.
Fold in the banana last. Serve at once, in small portions.
items.guidance: Eaten at Ugadi to carry all six tastes in one spoon — sweet, sour, salt, pungent, bitter and astringent — as a deliberate statement that the year holds all of them. It is the clearest household expression of sarva-rasa-abhyasa in the calendar. Ritual portion, not a meal.

items.name: Horse Gram Soup (Kulthi)
steps: Boil the soaked kulthi in plenty of water until soft, forty minutes or so; keep the cooking water.
Temper cumin, ginger and garlic in ghee and add to the pot with turmeric and pepper.
Simmer ten minutes more and serve as a thin broth rather than a thick dal.
items.guidance: Kulattha is the classical lekhana pulse — scraping, drying, kapha- and meda-reducing, and traditionally given for stones. Heating, so pitta should be careful. Vata: extra ghee. Pitta: reduce the ginger and garlic. Kapha: this is the indicated one.

items.name: Parwal Sabzi
steps: Scrape the parwal lightly and halve; leave the seeds in if tender.
Heat the mustard oil to smoking then cool slightly — this removes its raw pungency — and temper the cumin.
Add the parwal, turmeric, coriander and salt; cook covered on low heat until soft, turning once.
Finish with fresh coriander.
items.guidance: Patola is one of the few vegetables the samhitas call tridoshahara and specifically pathya during fever and convalescence. Light, easy to digest. Vata: cook soft with extra oil. Pitta: as written. Kapha: as written.

items.name: Tinda Sabzi
steps: Peel the tinda thinly and quarter; very young ones need no peeling.
Temper cumin and asafoetida in ghee, add turmeric and coriander.
Add the tinda with a splash of water, cover and cook on low until it collapses slightly, about fifteen minutes.
Salt at the end so it does not draw water early.
items.guidance: A summer gourd, cooling and light, in the same family as parwal and ash gourd. The asafoetida is there because gourds can be vata-provoking. Vata: cook very soft with extra ghee. Pitta: as written. Kapha: as written.
provenance: Punjabi and north Indian household tradition
